questiontext.text:
Find the antiderivatives or evaluate the definite integral

\(\displaystyle\int{@func@}\,d{@tt@}\)

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Let us solve \(\displaystyle \int {@func@}\, d{@tt@}\) by substitution method.

let \(u= \displaystyle {@us@} \)

Differentiating \(u\) with respect to \({@tt@}\) yields to \(\frac{du}{d{@tt@}}={@bb@}\). Then \(d{@tt@}=\frac{du}{@bb@}\)

Replacing \(u\) and \(d{@tt@}\) expressions into the original integral yields;

\[  \qquad \displaystyle \int {@func@}\, d{@tt@} = \displaystyle \int {@func_u@}\, du \]

\[\iff \displaystyle \int {@func@}\, d{@tt@} = \displaystyle \int {@func_u@}\, du \]

\[\iff \displaystyle \int {@func@}\, d{@tt@} = {@tas@} \]

Substituting the expression corresponding to \(u\) into \({@tas@}\) yields to:

\[ \displaystyle \int {@func@}\, d{@tt@} = {@ta_1@} \]
